pairs.description: Concomitant administration of kava and alprazolam has been documented to cause excessive central nervous system depression and semicomatose lethargy.
pairs.mechanism: Synergistic potentiation of central GABA-A receptor neurotransmission combined with kavalactone-mediated CYP inhibition.

pairs.description: Kava antagonizes the therapeutic antiparkinsonian efficacy of levodopa, precipitating acute worsening of motor symptoms and parkinsonism.
pairs.mechanism: Central dopamine D2 receptor antagonism by kavalactones interfering with striatal dopaminergic neurotransmission.

pairs.description: Kava significantly intensifies the sedative, hypnotic, and motor-impairing effects of barbiturates, benzodiazepines, and central depressants.
pairs.mechanism: Additive central nervous system depressant activity through positive allosteric modulation of GABA-A receptors.

pairs.description: Combining kava with hepatotoxic medications like acetaminophen dramatically increases the risk of severe drug-induced liver injury and hepatic necrosis.
pairs.mechanism: Depletion of hepatic glutathione stores by kavalactones compounding toxic NAPQI metabolite accumulation from acetaminophen.
